execution.trigger: When init is called with v > k
execution.state_issue: The subtraction of a larger value from a smaller one does not result in an underflow but wraps around to a large positive number.
execution.exploitable_behavior: map[k] stores incorrect values due to integer wrapping.

causality.state: k and v are uint256, so their subtraction can't directly cause negative numbers without wrapping.
causality.guard: No bounds checking on v > k.
causality.transition: Subtraction wraps around when underflow occurs.
causality.capability: Attacker provides v > k to exploit incorrect map values.
causality.outcome: map[k] stores unintended large positive values.
